transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. I am sorry to hear that. Running a microwave empty for 10 minutes is very likely to have caused internal damage. The magnetron needs food or water inside it to absorb the energy; without anything there, the energy reflects back into the components, causing them to overheat rapidly. The "horrible smell" you are experiencing is probably burning insulation, plastic, or the mica (waveguide) cover inside the cavity. Because this involves high-voltage internal components and potential fire damage, I must advise you to stop using the appliance immediately. Do not try to run it again to see if the smell clears, as this could cause further damage or a safety hazard. Please unplug the microwave from the mains socket now. If you are comfortable doing so with the appliance unplugged, you might check if the small rectangular cover on the inside wall (the waveguide cover) looks burnt or blackened, but do not attempt any repairs yourself.

Thanks. It's turned off at the switch but still plugged in. I'll pull the plug now. There was some smoke from the side vents when we stopped it, and a brownish mark on the side wall inside. Is it safe, or should I bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
It is not safe to use. The combination of smoke from the vents and a brownish mark inside indicates that an internal component has overheated or burned. This could be the waveguide cover (the mica panel), the magnetron, or internal wiring insulation. Do not plug it back in or try to run it again. Even if the smell seems faint now, there may be hidden damage or carbon tracking that could cause a fire or electric shock later. You should have it checked by a qualified engineer before considering reuse. Given the severity of running it empty for 10 minutes and the visible smoke/mark, repair costs often exceed the value of older microwaves, so you might consider replacement instead. If you do choose to repair, ensure the engineer replaces any burnt components (like the waveguide cover) and checks the magnetron.

candidates: Internal damage from dry running (magnetron, HV transformer, or waveguide cover) (high)
